name: Swing Pullback — fix 1 (trailing-edge market filter)
plain_words: The Swing Pullback, but a market is only traded while its own last three years of these trades (the ones already closed) show a profit. No market is dropped by hand — the rule drops it, in time, with no look-ahead. Answers the first test's lesson: Bitcoin lost, gold and Nasdaq worked.
related: FAST_TRADES_REPORT killed 2-5 day dip buys AS THE BOOK'S TIMING SIGNAL (a replacement for the 150-day line). This is a different thing: a separate trade with its own stop, target and time exit, judged in R. Declared as such.

data.source: repo data/daily.csv (fetch.py: Yahoo QQQ/GLD, Kraken BTC)

costs_bps.note: round trip in basis points of notional: QQQ as MNQ ($1.22 + 2 ticks), gold as MGC, Bitcoin as Kraken spot taker 0.20% per side

firm.name: FTMO US Swing $100k (holds overnight and over weekends)
firm.note: swing holds cannot run on a flat-by-close futures firm; the venue for 1-7 day holds is the Swing account

pass_line.note: tightened 2026-09-14 before any verdict was adopted: 'sized so the firm's rules hold' is evaluated as the LARGEST risk per trade at which they hold, and the strategy must earn >= 10%/yr of the account at that size — an edge that only survives at a size that earns nothing is not a pass

expectation: Bitcoin drops out once its losing stretch is visible; expectancy per trade rises; but the 2021 hole came from all three markets at once, so the worst stretch probably stays deep and the return at the surviving size stays under 10%/yr. Likely still FAIL. This is fix 1 of 3 for the family.
